technical_note.name: level2_threshold_boundary_and_critical_seed_hypothesis
technical_note.purpose: Preserve the interpretation that Level-2 collapse timing differences may indicate approach to an admissibility boundary, and define a detailed simulation program to test that idea.

core_claim.statement: The current Level-2 results are consistent with a thresholded continuation boundary: initial structure changes how long the dynamics remain near an admissible continuation corridor, but the tested parameter point still lies in a collapse regime.
core_claim.strong_form_if_confirmed: Level-2 contains a critical basin-coherence threshold separating subcritical collapse from sustained bounded continuation.
core_claim.safe_current_form: The results suggest a near-threshold regime with long-lived transients and initial-condition sensitivity, but do not yet prove a true critical seed or a formal saddle-node bifurcation.

observed_interpretation.near_uniform_noise: Likely misses or fails to assemble an admissible continuation corridor; collapse is rapid.
observed_interpretation.localized_seed: Temporarily assembles a basin-like structure; continuation survives longer before losing admissibility.
observed_interpretation.front_seeded: Begins closest to a coherent continuation corridor; survives longest, then collapses.

threshold_language.preferred_term: minimum basin coherence required for sustained continuation
avoid_overclaiming: Do not yet say 'proved critical seed size'
Do not yet say 'collapse is only a metric artifact'

classes.name: global_admissibility_failure
classes.description: No persistent basin forms; collapse occurs quickly.

classes.name: transient_basin_interface_destabilization
classes.description: A basin forms and supports continuation transiently, but later loses admissibility.

classes.name: bounded_continuation
classes.description: A finite-width active interface persists for long times with bounded metrics.

theoretical_taxonomy.working_hypothesis: The current anchor point lies in C1/C2 territory, near a boundary beyond which C3 may exist.

hypotheses.name: critical_basin_coherence_hypothesis
hypotheses.statement: There exists a minimum coherent seed configuration below which continuation always fails and above which a persistent basin can survive.

hypotheses.name: near_threshold_transient_hypothesis
hypotheses.statement: Long-lived transients at the current parameter point reflect proximity to a lost or barely inaccessible admissible continuation branch.

hypotheses.name: projection_limit_hypothesis
hypotheses.statement: Some observed collapse may reflect loss of representability of the basin in the projection variables rather than immediate disappearance of the deeper process structure.

overall_design.goal: Differentiate true regime collapse, thresholded continuation, and projection-limited collapse.

required_checks.name: dead_domain_test
required_checks.spec: Initialize epsilon≈0, rho≈0, residue≈0 everywhere. Verify excluded_active_fraction does not falsely approach 1.

required_checks.name: stationary_interface_test
required_checks.spec: Construct a smooth stationary two-region interface. Verify nonzero interface count, finite width, near-zero velocity.

required_checks.name: traveling_front_surrogate
required_checks.spec: Use a controlled synthetic front position sequence or a parameter set known to advect a front. Verify velocity extraction is sensible.

required_checks.name: negative_blowup_test
required_checks.spec: Inject or induce a large negative excursion. Verify symmetric invalid detection catches it.

required_checks.name: malformed_input_test
required_checks.spec: Pass state arrays with wrong length. Verify immediate explicit failure.

P1_anchor_reconfirmation.purpose: Reconfirm the present result under frozen metrics.
P1_anchor_reconfirmation.success_condition: Reproduce qualitative ordering: near_uniform_noise collapses fastest; structured ICs survive longer; endpoint class remains collapse.

P2_parameter_threshold_search.purpose: Search for an admissibility boundary in parameter space.
P2_parameter_threshold_search.strategy: One-parameter coarse sweeps first, holding all other parameters fixed at anchor values.

lam.rationale: Likely strongest control on exclusion completion vs survivability.

kappa.rationale: Likely strong control on front sharpening or rigidity.

gamma.rationale: Likely strong control on redistribution / damping balance.

D_eps.rationale: Tests whether wider exclusion fronts suppress singular collapse.

D_rho.rationale: Tests whether continuation support / smoothing shifts the regime.

P2_parameter_threshold_search.expected_signature_of_boundary: Collapse time grows sharply over a narrow parameter interval, with structured ICs showing stronger lifetime extension near the boundary.

P3_seed_threshold_search.purpose: Test whether a true critical seed / basin-coherence threshold exists.

decision_rule.subcritical: All runs collapse and collapse_time remains finite without trend toward persistence.
decision_rule.marginal: Collapse_time increases strongly and interface survives for long transients.
decision_rule.supercritical_candidate: Interface persists over late window with bounded width and nonzero active fraction.

critical_seed_evidence: A narrow transition in survival time as radius or width changes
A switch from universal collapse to persistent continuation over a small parameter increment
Strong critical slowing-down near the threshold

P4_resolution_scaling.purpose: Test whether observed collapse is a real process regime or a projection/representation limit.

interpretation.if_collapse_time_increases_with_resoluti: Representation scale may be suppressing or erasing real basin continuation.
interpretation.if_qualitative_behavior_is_resolution_in: Collapse is more likely a true regime property of the modeled dynamics.

P5_long_run_validation_of_candidate_wind.purpose: Confirm whether candidate persistent regimes are truly bounded continuation rather than delayed collapse.
P5_long_run_validation_of_candidate_wind.trigger: Only after P2 or P3 reveals a candidate C3 window.
P5_long_run_validation_of_candidate_wind.success_condition: Finite-width interface persists across extended late-time window with bounded velocity and no invalid termination.

common_numerical_requirements.boundary_conditions: Keep identical across all scan phases; document explicitly in batch config.
common_numerical_requirements.grid_policy: Do not change grid convention mid-study.
common_numerical_requirements.snapshot_schedule: Use fixed save cadence across comparison runs.
common_numerical_requirements.stability_policy: Record dt, Nx, runtime, save interval, and any CFL-like constraints for every run.

signs: active_fraction drops strongly or interface never stabilizes
nonzero interface persists for meaningful transient
late-time collapse to interface loss or activity death
finite front width bounded away from zero

must_generate.purpose: One row per run with class assignment and key late-time metrics.

must_generate.name: regime_map.csv
must_generate.purpose: Parameter-grid summary showing dominant class by setting.

must_generate.name: critical_seed_scan.csv
must_generate.purpose: Tracks seed radius/width/amplitude versus persistence outcome.

evidence_for_near_threshold_behavior: Sharp increase in collapse time over a narrow parameter interval
Much stronger IC sensitivity near the same interval
Marginal runs with long plateaus before failure
evidence_for_true_critical_seed: A narrow seed-size or seed-width boundary separating universal collapse from sustained continuation
Persistence that survives longer runtime and higher resolution
evidence_for_projection_limited_collapse: Candidate persistent basins become longer-lived or survive when Nx is increased
Front width relative to grid spacing is a strong predictor of collapse
evidence_for_true_regime_collapse: Qualitative collapse ordering is stable under resolution increase
No candidate persistent regime emerges even after threshold scans
All IC classes remain endpoint-invariant while only transients change

safe_theoretical_statements_for_paper: The current Level-2 results indicate that the tested parameter point lies in a collapse regime with strong initial-condition effects on transient lifetime but not on the final endpoint.

This behavior is consistent with proximity to an admissibility boundary where structured initial conditions can temporarily support basin-like continuation without preventing eventual exclusion completion.
A targeted threshold-search program is required to determine whether the system supports a true critical basin-coherence threshold and a bounded continuation regime.
Resolution scaling is necessary to distinguish true process collapse from collapse induced by loss of representability in the projected simulation variables.
unsafe_statements_to_avoid_for_now: The system definitely has a saddle-node bifurcation.
A true critical seed size has already been discovered.
The observed collapse is only a metric artifact.
The process itself terminates whenever the projection collapses.

recommended_next_actions.action: Freeze metric schema and threshold config.
Run P2 lam sweep first, classify all runs.
Choose the longest-transient parameter neighborhood and run P3 seed-threshold search there.
Run P4 resolution scaling on anchor, marginal, and best-candidate cases.

technical_note.one_sentence_summary: The Level-2 results are best treated as evidence for a possible thresholded admissibility boundary: structured initial conditions appear to buy temporary access to a continuation corridor, and the next simulation program should determine whether that corridor can become a true bounded regime under changed parameters, stronger seed coherence, or improved resolution.
